blueprint_concepts: Position vector, distance formula, section formula
english: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be the lines $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-4}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{2}$ respectively. Let $P$ be a point on $L_1$ and $Q$ be a point on $L_2$ such that the mid-point of the line segment $PQ$ is $\left(4,\dfrac{9}{4},6\right)$. Then the length of $PQ$ is ______.
hindi: माना $L_1$ तथा $L_2$ क्रमशः रेखाएँ $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$ तथा $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-4}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{2}$ हैं। माना $L_1$ पर एक बिन्दु $P$ तथा $L_2$ पर एक बिन्दु $Q$ इस प्रकार हैं कि रेखाखण्ड $PQ$ का मध्यबिन्दु $\left(4,\dfrac{9}{4},6\right)$ है। तब $PQ$ की लम्बाई ______ है।
solution: First and third: $s+2t=7,\ 2s+2t=9\Rightarrow s=2,\ t=\dfrac52$; second: $3+4-\dfrac52=\dfrac92$, consistent
solution_full: Writing each symmetric equation equal to a parameter, a general point of $L_1$ is $P=(2+s,\,-1+2s,\,3+2s)$ and a general point of $L_2$ is $Q=(-1+2t,\,4-t,\,2t)$, $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$.
By the section (mid-point) formula, the mid-point of $PQ$ is $\left(\dfrac{1+s+2t}{2},\dfrac{3+2s-t}{2},\dfrac{3+2s+2t}{2}\right)$.
Subtracting the first from the third gives $s=2$; then $t=\dfrac52$.
These satisfy the second equation: $2(2)-\dfrac52=\dfrac32$. So the three equations are consistent and the solution is unique (the directions of $L_1$, $L_2$ are not parallel).
originality_note: New: a segment with one end on each of two non-intersecting lines is fixed by its mid-point; three mid-point equations in two parameters must be consistent and give the ends (way 3, an object defined by two conditions). Closest known: in two dimensions, 'line through a point bisected between two lines'. Different because: in space the mid-point condition gives an over-determined linear system, and no line through the mid-point is asked for.

concept_use.Position vector, distance formula, secti: Mid-point (section) formula for PQ gives three linear equations; the distance formula gives PQ = 2.5.
concept_use.Equation of a line: Converting the symmetric (Cartesian) equations of L1 and L2 to general points with parameters s and t.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, vector and point is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that the three mid-point equations in the two parameters are consistent, so P and Q exist, and that they are unique because the lines are not parallel; 'line segment PQ' and the coordinates are explicit. Changed: No change.
key_step: Writing general points of the two lines and solving the mid-point equations (checking the third for consistency).
justification: Routine chain of standard steps: parametric points, mid-point formula, a linear system and a distance. No insight, so Level 2, like 2026-P2-Q1 (L2) and 2024-P1-Q16 items.
